name: Ultramarine Debt

description: Ultramarine Debt is a seam of deep blue light stitched across half an astronomical unit, as though spacetime were cloth torn on a nail. Starlight splits along its length into before-images and after-images, both equally vivid. Sensors routinely report weapons fire, engine burns, and distress calls that have yet to happen.

Near the seam, consequences arrive early: replies precede questions, and alarms sound for impacts that land minutes later. Crossing into the corridor, crews encounter themselves — calm, rehearsed versions walking slightly out of step with the present. The seam widens without rhythm, and its growth has accelerated every decade since recording began.

In 2317 the destroyer Kettleblack engaged an unidentified raider, then received her own distress call dated three days hence, recounting the battle in the past tense. Twelve ships have entered the widest fold; forty-one distinct wrecks have since been catalogued leaving it. Underwriters quietly refuse to insure passage, which tells merchants more than any survey.

Fleet doctrine now forbids engagement within ten light-minutes of the seam, though the seam itself has begun answering hails with voices claiming to be the hails' authors. Research stations at safe distance collect pre-arriving telemetry, publishing tomorrow's news in fragments. Sailors say the Debt always balances — you simply pay before you borrow.
